description: Exp3 iter-4 critique of position_decaying_example_evidence — 8 stats (rule-violating interior, rule-matching, up/down 1ex, Weber edge, prefix re-test, 2ex gap fill, 4ex-2ex interior, multiples of lone example); iter-3 got 1/8 (prefix)

- rule_matching_target_yes 0.96 (n=125)

- fourth_example_prefix_broadening 0.287

name: exp3-iter3-position-decaying-evidence
description: Exp3 iter-3 cand_0 — example evidence scaled exp(rho*(k-1)) has rho≈+0.015 (null); with an equal range prior it ties the incumbent at MAP; exact sparse (set, coverage-pattern, width) class tabulation gives 14 ms/grad
metadata:
  type: project
---
Exp3 iter 3, candidate_0 (2026-10-31), exploratory order slot. Submitted `position_decaying_example_evidence`: each example's log-evidence is scaled by exp(rho*(k-1)) (total not conserved), the range prior is equal (no Weber, heading or upward terms), sampling is with replacement, plus digit sums and a lapse.
- MAP on the incumbent base (exact grid): rho=0 gives -3189.44, free rho gives -3188.65 (rho +0.02). Weber+heading+upward together are worth only about 1 nat.
- The submitted model's MAP is -3190.47 against the incumbent's -3190.30, with 3 fewer parameters. Its pool RMSE is at least 0.0059 vs the incumbent, heading_weber, digit_sum_open_ended and example_blind_lapse. The smoke fit gave -3192.4.
- So rho does not capture the prefix-extension critique: the decay comes out null.
Speed trick: under an equal range prior, an interval's evidence depends only on its (contiguous sorted-example coverage pattern, width). Flatten the nonzero (set, pattern, width) classes (~67k) and the (cell, class) entries (~268k) and use inc_subtensor segment sums. That is 14 ms/grad, exact; the dense 100x100 grid took 310 ms.
PITFALL: compile_fn on raw module-level tensors draws the RVs at random; use model.replace_rvs_by_values first.
See [[exp3-iter3-critique]], [[number-game-ceiling]].

name: exp3-iter3-set-size-evidence
description: Exp3 iter-3 cand_4 — set-size-scaled evidence (n/2.5)^-rho on the WR incumbent +1.35 MAP, RMSE 0.0088; stray-by-size/position null; 4-D Taylor (evidence axis) speed trick
metadata:
  type: project
---
Exp3 iter 3, cand_4 (2026-10-31), refinement slot on heading_weber_upward_with_replacement. The base MAP LL is -3190.30.

MAP screens:
- stray rate by set size: +0.2
- position-graded stray rate: +0.1
- last-example trust: +0.06
- evidence scaled by (n/2.5)^-rho: +1.35 (rho=-0.068, so larger sets weigh more per example; this runs opposite to the prefix-extension critique). Pool RMSE 0.0088.

Submitted `set_size_scaled_evidence`. Smoke -3192.4.

Speed: a dense softmax over 5113 hypotheses is about 85 ms per gradient, too slow. Instead, add a 4th Taylor axis in (w-1)*(ll-scale)/10 to the incumbent's moments. With K_G=7, K_R=6, K_E=7 it takes 13.7 ms and is exact to 1e-8 at MAP. With K=12/10/10 the GEMMs were memory-bound at 76 ms.

The screening script is at iter_3/candidate_4/scratch/s/screen.py. See [[exp3-iter2-rule-breadth-graft]], [[fit-speed-budget]].

name: exp3-iter3-trend-origin-room
description: Exp3 iter-3 cand_5 — prefix stat is one set pair; trust slope / set-size lapse null; sample-size neglect and per-set stray schedules lose 50-110 nats; first→last trend heading swap submitted (smoke -3192.7)
metadata:
  type: project
---
Exp3 iter 3, candidate_5 (2026-10-31), refinement slot. Base: heading_weber_with_upward_counting, MAP obs LL -3190.24.

- The prefix_extension critique stat rests on a single pair: 31,3,1 → 31,3,1,15 (15 targets, yes rate 0.33 → 0.62). Not worth building a mechanism around.
- Position-graded trust, using an exact expansion over subsets of genuine examples: slope 0.047, +0.14 nats, and 65 ms per gradient (7x the base). Null, and too slow.
- Lapse rate as a logistic function of set size: slope -0.05, null.
- Tempering by a fixed set-size schedule (sample-size neglect): min(n,3) -53, n^0.8 -49, 1+log n -150.
- Stray rate is sharp at 0.9. Per-set stray schedule 0.9^(1/n): -113. 1-0.1n/2.5: -38. Constant 0.85: -30. Constant 0.93: -15.
- Submitted: heading = sign(last - first) in place of the last step. MAP -3190.06, beta -0.13, read as "the run started partway into the range". Named `trend_origin_room_upward_counting`, smoke -3192.7, about 15 s.
**How to apply:** the stray and evidence-weight dimensions are saturated on exp3, so don't re-screen them. See [[exp3-iter3-critique]], [[exp3-iter2-rule-breadth-graft]].

metadata:

  originSessionId: 1d82c78b-0bac-4618-97c8-da7bd32baa1b

---

Admission fits use production draws 4000 + tune 3000 per chain (warm_start_nuts, dense mass matrix), 30-min limit per run. Machine has 1 core. Incumbent `tenenbaum_digit_concepts` logp+grad ≈ 12 ms. A memory-subset mixture over its hypothesis space (≈700 states) cost 62 ms naive → too slow (~49 min).

**Why:** the check_candidate smoke fit (200 iters) passes even when the full fit would time out.

**How to apply:** benchmark logp+dlogp time and NUTS n_steps (probe `_warm_start_sample` with small draws) before finishing. Speedups that worked: replace gathering posterior rows per cell (slow AdvancedIncSubtensor1 gradient) with a `pytensor.sparse.CSR` + `structured_dot` (44→25 ms); declaring module-level `SAMPLER_SETTINGS = {"target_accept": 0.9}` halves steps (10.8→5.3). Don't name a scratch script `timeit.py` (shadows stdlib, breaks pymc import). Related: [[digit-concepts-key]].

Also worked (2026-10-30, `order_weighted_concept_learning`): when intervals must be grouped by (size, per-position hit pattern) instead of (size, k), keep only each set's non-empty groups (≤473 of 1600 on this data) padded per set, and gather size-dependent terms by index — 47 → 18 ms.

content.content:
"""Heading, Weber width and upward counting with evidence weighted by set size.

Refinement of `heading_weber_upward_with_replacement`: people do Bayesian
concept learning over 45 arithmetic and digit rules, the 18 digit-sum concepts
(an inferred family share) and every interval of 1..100, reading the examples as
independent draws (with replacement) with 10% strays and a guessing lapse, with
a Weber range-width prior (width / midpoint)^gamma, ranges stretched toward the
last step's heading and credited by their room above the largest example. The
one change is that the weight people give the evidence depends on how many
examples were shown: the log-likelihood of an n-example set enters belief scaled
by n^(-kappa) (kappa inferred), so single examples are judged as before, while
larger sets sharpen belief toward small concepts by more (kappa < 0) or by less
(kappa > 0) than an ideal learner.

The interval part keeps the incumbent's Taylor-moment tabulation, with one more

digit-sum concepts (an inferred family share) and every interval of 1..100, with
the best model's range prior: Weber-like relative width, a stretch toward the
last step's heading, and credit for room above the largest example. Examples are

The one change is in attention. When people weigh a stretch of the number line,
they attend only to the smallest and the largest example, which mark where the
stretch must reach, and do not count the examples in between as further evidence

from scipy.special import logsumexp

I submitted `interior_example_range_weight`. It passes the admission check (smoke log-likelihood -3193.5), but it will probably be rejected as a near-duplicate of `heading_weber_upward_with_replacement`.

**What it claims.** It refines the pruned `outermost_examples_range_evidence`, which lost by 184 nats because it gave the in-between examples no weight when judging how wide a range is. In the new version the smallest and largest examples count in full, and the in-between ones count at an inferred weight ω. Rule and digit-sum evidence still uses every example. The rest of the learner is `heading_weber_upward_with_replacement`. This bears on the critique's one case, 31,3,1 → 31,3,1,15, where the fourth example falls inside the span.

**Why it will likely collapse onto its parent.** In my quick best-fit screens, ω comes out at 1 (no change), so the model's predictions nearly match `heading_weber_upward_with_replacement`'s. Every other change I screened on the rank-1 model (`set_size_scaled_evidence_weight`, -3188.1 at its best fit) was either null or lost:

| Change | Result |
|---|---|
| Separate prior weight on odd/even rules | +0.02 nats, null |
| Shift between rules and ranges with set size | null |
| Lapse that rises when the examples fit no concept well | lapse goes to about 0, null |
| Log-odds response map instead of the guess lapse | predictions differ from the parent by RMSE 0.002, a duplicate |
| Examples drawn without replacement | RMSE 0.0006 against `heading_weber_with_upward_counting`, a duplicate |
| At most one stray example per set | 77 nats worse |
| Strays drawn only from numbers outside the concept | 24 nats worse |

On the critique pair, the rank-1 model predicts "yes" to even numbers rising from 0.24 to 0.42 after 15 is added; people went from about 0.2 to 0.6. That gap rests on one set pair with 5 responses per target. Across all set–target pairs the misfit is about what binomial sampling noise alone would give, so I found nothing systematic left to model.

**Speed.** One gradient takes about 17 ms, which should keep each admission run under the 30-minute limit. The smoke fit initially failed because the check evaluates parameter values where the model's series approximation goes negative. I added guards against that, and it now passes.

The three files are in `iter_4/candidate_5/`, and I saved the screen results to memory so they aren't repeated.
